title: Production Security Audits
learning_outcomes: Explain what production security audits contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: dependency vulnerability checks.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. In this lesson, focus on dependency vulnerability checks; then compare it with php configuration review. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use production security audits when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Security begins at trust boundaries. Validate data for the intended operation, encode output for its exact context, constrain file and network access, protect credentials, and apply authorization consistently. For production security audits, begin with dependency vulnerability checks. Also distinguish php configuration review; least-privilege permissions; security logging and incident response. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Dependency vulnerability checks
items.text: Keep package metadata and source layout consistent, and verify version constraints and class-to-file mapping with the selected tools.

items.title: PHP configuration review
items.text: Know when to use php configuration review, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

items.title: Least-privilege permissions
items.text: Distinguish identity verification from resource permission, and test expiry, invalid credentials, and denied access as well as the success path.

items.title: Security logging and incident response
items.text: Track where this value enters the request lifecycle and where it affects the response; client-provided data must be treated as untrusted.

items.title: Regular upgrades and patch management
items.text: Know when to use regular upgrades and patch management, what input or program state it changes, and which boundary case is worth testing.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Validate data at system boundaries and encode output for the target context; validation and escaping solve different problems.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for production security audits from top to bottom. Start by identifying dependency vulnerability checks, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for production security audits that demonstrates "dependency vulnerability checks". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of dependency vulnerability checks.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating input validation as output escaping.
common_mistakes.why: A value can be valid data and still be unsafe in an HTML or JavaScript output context.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate shape and business rules at input boundaries, then apply context-appropriate output encoding.

common_mistakes.why: A request can be sent without the original form or browser UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Repeat all security-relevant validation and authorization on the server.

common_mistakes.problem: Returning internal error details to the browser.
common_mistakes.why: Stack traces and configuration values may expose sensitive information.
common_mistakes.fix: Log safe diagnostics server-side and return a generic, useful response.

summary: Production Security Audits is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Validate data at system boundaries and encode output for the target context; validation and escaping solve different problems.
